name: aiops
description: AI operations: an ops inventory (hosts, services, SLOs, alert rules, maintenance windows), monitoring (Prometheus, Loki or docker logs, probes, host stats, Docker; Grafana dashboards, alert rules and annotations; Tempo and Jaeger traces; a service dependency graph; statistical anomaly detection on metrics and log patterns), ssh with Key Vault credentials and pinned host keys, alert checks and SLO burn rates, incidents and postmortems with an evidence ledger and incident memory (similar past incidents), safe runbooks, the incident-response and ops-advisor workflows, SRE agents and skills, and the runbook-safe, inventory-valid, alerts-valid and ops-healthy gates. Its tools appear in sessions whose workspace has .harness/ops/inventory.yaml (or when the operator sets HARNESS_OPS_INVENTORY). It reaches the hosts and endpoints the inventory names directly - that is its job; only the operator's inventory attaches Key Vault credentials (to its hosts and endpoints), every call that uses one is asked about (vault rules), and the server's own Docker engine is off unless the operator allows containers. In the desktop: an Operations console (incidents with their timeline, evidence, root cause, refuter verdict, runbook and postmortem; firing alerts; services with health and SLOs; the dependency topology; the change timeline), an On call home card, status items, /incident, /investigate and /ops-check.

views.title: Operations
views.description: On call at a glance: open incidents, firing alerts, SLO error budgets, service health, quick actions.

views.title: Incidents
views.description: Open and recent incidents: severity, service, status and age; each with its timeline, evidence, root cause, refuter verdict, runbook and postmortem.

views.title: Services
views.description: The inventory: health and SLO status of each service.

views.title: Topology
views.description: What depends on what, with each service's health.

views.title: Changes
views.description: Deploys, rollouts, applies, CI runs, commits, restarts and runbooks, newest first.

agent.description: Opens an incident on the Operations page: its timeline, alerts, evidence, root cause and confidence, the refuter verdict, the runbook and the postmortem. id is an alert incident (alr-...) or an incident record (inc-...).

id.description: The incident id, alr-... or inc-...

agent.description: Evaluates every alert rule of the server inventory now (PromQL, probes, health URLs; no model, no credentials) and shows the person how many fire.

slashCommands.name: incident
slashCommands.description: Open an incident and triage it

action.prompt:
Open an incident for: {args}

Use the incident tool (action open: a title, the severity by user impact, the affected services, a summary), then triage it read-only with ops_check, slo_status and the recent changes, and add what you find to its timeline with the evidence ids.
Investigate this with the incident-response workflow (symptom: {args}). Change nothing without my approval.

slashCommands.name: ops-check
slashCommands.description: Evaluate the alert rules now (no model)

schema.title: Operations console
schema.description: How the Operations pages look on this computer. The server's own watch loop runs on its schedule (HARNESS_OPS_WATCH_SECONDS); here you choose how often the pages look.

refreshSeconds.title: Watch interval (seconds)
refreshSeconds.description: How often the pages, the home card and the badges refresh.

minSeverity.title: Alert severity minimum
minSeverity.description: Alerts below it are left out of the Alerts page and the counts.

schema.title: Investigations
schema.description: The models an investigation you start from the Operations pages uses: kept with your account. Another model than the conversation's is a delegation, used only when your delegation setting (Settings > Agents) allows it.

evidenceModel.title: Model for gathering evidence
evidenceModel.description: The evidence steps of an investigation you start here. Empty: the conversation's model. Another model is a delegation, used only when your delegation setting (Settings > Agents) allows it.

refuterModel.title: Model for the refuter
refuterModel.description: A second opinion from another provider before anything changes. Empty: the conversation's model. A delegation, as above.
